title: Set two classroom projectors at the throw distance that fills each screen
instruction: Set up the two projectors for the two screens on the front wall, one projector per screen. Each screen is 160 mm wide (1.6 m at this 1:10 scale). The black projector has a 1.5:1 throw ratio and the white one 1.0:1 (throw distance, from the front of the lens to the screen = throw ratio x picture width). Stand each projector upright on the table facing its screen, square to the wall, its lens on the screen's centre line, at the distance where its picture just fills the screen.
context: Audio and video technicians and school IT and AV staff set up portable projectors in classrooms, lecture rooms and meeting rooms. A fixed-lens projector's throw ratio is printed by its maker: throw distance (from the front of the lens to the screen) = throw ratio x picture width. To fill a 1.6 m screen a 1.5:1 projector stands 2.4 m from it and a 1.0:1 short-throw projector 1.6 m, so two different projectors for two identical screens stand at different distances. The lens must also be on the screen's centre line and the projector square to the wall, or the picture is shifted off the screen and keystoned into a trapezoid (digital keystone correction costs sharpness). Working out the distance from the ratio, setting it with a tape and squaring the projector to the wall is the technician's routine before a session. Here the room is at 1:10.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the floor of the front of a classroom at 1:10 scale. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases (toward the front wall), y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Fixed: (1) Front wall: a pale green painted MDF board 10 mm thick (x 47.0 to 48.0 cm), 500 mm wide (y -25.0 to +25.0 cm) and 190 mm tall. (2) Two projection screens: matt white PVC sheets 2 mm thick flat on the wall's face (x 46.8 to 47.0 cm; their faces at x 46.8 cm), each 160 mm wide (1.6 m at scale) and 100 mm tall (80 to 180 mm up); the left screen centred on y +12.0 cm (y +4.0 to +20.0 cm), the right on y -12.0 cm (y -20.0 to -4.0 cm), 80 mm of wall between them. (3) Centre marks: a black PVC strip 4 mm wide, 60 mm tall (15 to 75 mm up) and 2 mm thick on the wall's face below each screen's centre (y +12.0 and -12.0 cm). (4) Projector table: classroom tables pushed together, a beech-effect laminate block 200 mm (x 17.0 to 37.0 cm) by 400 mm (y -20.0 to +20.0 cm) and 75 mm tall (0.75 m); its far edge is 98 mm from the screens. Loose: (5) Two portable projectors, each one rigid 50 g body: a box 34 mm across, 26 mm front to back and 14 mm tall, with a lens barrel (a box 14 mm across and 10 mm tall, centred on the front face at mid-height) standing 5 mm proud of the front face; outline seen from above 31 mm front to back (lens included) by 34 mm across. One is black ABS with a silver lens, throw ratio 1.5:1; the other white ABS with a black lens, throw ratio 1.0:1 (both fixed lenses, no zoom). The throw distance is measured from the centre of the lens's front face. Start: both standing on the table, turned sideways with their lenses toward the middle: the black projector's body centred at x 30.0 cm, y +15.0 cm, lens toward -y; the white one's at x 30.0 cm, y -15.0 cm, lens toward +y (lens tips 264 mm apart). Nothing else is on the table. For a picture 160 mm wide the black projector's lens belongs 240 mm from its screen (at x 22.8 cm) and the white one's 160 mm (at x 30.8 cm).
scoring: The score is read at the last step from the projectors' poses, as a tape from the wall, a set square and a top photo would read them, and from each gripper's opening and finger positions. For each projector: its throw distance is how far the centre of its lens's front face is in front of the screens' faces (x 46.8 cm), measured square to the wall; its picture width is that distance divided by its own throw ratio (1.5 for the black projector, 1.0 for the white); its squareness is the angle, seen from above, between its lens's axis and straight at the wall; its centre-line offset is how far the centre of its lens is, sideways, from the nearer screen's centre line (y +12.0 or -12.0 cm). Standing: upright (tilted 5 degrees or less), on the projector table (the middle of its base over the table, its lowest point within 3 mm of the table's top), still (the middle of its base moved under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s, turns counted at its corners) and let go by both grippers: each is at least 90 % open (fingers 84.5 mm apart) or its fingers are more than 10 mm from the projector (the fingers taken as a zone round the gripper's axis from the finger tips 38 mm up, out to a pad's outer corner: radius 16 mm closed, 57 mm open); on a step where the grippers cannot be read, nothing is let go. A projector is set up for a screen when it is standing, its lens toward the wall within 10 degrees of square and its lens's centre within 12 mm of that screen's centre line. It earns 0.5 if, as well, it is square within 5 degrees, its lens within 6 mm of the centre line and its picture within 5 % of the screen's 160 mm (152 to 168 mm: a throw of 228 to 252 mm for the 1.5:1 projector, 152 to 168 mm for the 1.0:1); 0.25 if its picture is within 15 % (136 to 184 mm: a throw of 204 to 276 mm, or 136 to 184 mm) but it misses one or more of those three; else 0. A projector that is not standing (tipped, lifted, moving or still held), is turned more than 10 degrees from square (sideways as at the start, or lens toward the arms after a turn the wrong way), is off both centre lines, or makes a picture more than 15 % too wide or too narrow earns nothing. Each screen counts its best projector once, and the score is the sum for the two screens: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0; the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Either projector may serve either screen (the screens are the same width), judged on the distance its own ratio needs: 240 mm for the black, 160 mm for the white. Examples: the start 0; both right 1.0; one right and the other 20 mm too far (picture 173 mm for the black, 180 mm for the white) 0.75; both 20 mm too far 0.5; one right and the other turned the wrong way, lens to the back, 0.5; one 20 mm too far and the other left at the start 0.25; both on one screen 0.5; each at the other's distance (the black at 160 mm, the white at 240 mm: pictures 107 and 240 mm) 0. In a real trial: a tape from the screen's face to the lens, a set square against the wall, a top photo for the centre line and the video for letting go.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The wall, screens, marks and table are fixed. Each projector is one rigid body of two boxes with no light, power, zoom, lens shift or keystone correction: the picture width is computed from the lens's distance and the stated throw ratio, as the maker's throw formula gives it. 'Let go' reads each gripper's opening and finger-tip point from the simulator (fingers taken as round about its axis). Masses are those of light scale models.
reset_notes: Stand the black projector with its body centred at x 30.0 cm, y +15.0 cm, its lens toward -y (toward the middle), and the white projector with its body centred at x 30.0 cm, y -15.0 cm, its lens toward +y, both upright on the projector table. Everything else is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
